assets.fullPrompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: original pixel-art scene concept board for a medieval low-fantasy RPG mod, not a finished game screenshot. 1536x1024 landscape requested.
Create exactly TWO side-by-side panels separated by a thick charcoal gutter, fixed identical camera, showing TWO successive staging poses of the SAME small voluntary hearing. No text anywhere.
Style: restrained dense pixel art, clearly readable hard-edged clusters, muted gray stone, old brown wood, olive wool, cream canvas and dull teal, three-quarter elevated RPG view. No blur, glossy 3D, neon or photographic faces.
Setting in both panels: a modest neutral quarantine-camp public hearing shelter in marshland, cream canvas roof on wood posts, rough stone ground, closed locked private case cabinet at rear, modest table with anonymous short mark sheets, no names. Wide OPEN foreground-left exit with an uninterrupted stone path, visible outside daylight, no gate or guards. Keep furniture, papers, exit and camera identical across panels. Seating is sparse, not a crowd.
Exactly THREE people per panel: Morlen, a gray-haired full gray-bearded older retired medic in olive long coat, cream neck scarf, brown shoulder medical satchel; a generic receiving caregiver, dark tied hair, olive dress, brown apron, cream cloth at belt (NOT named Mia); one generic adult voluntary patient-questioner in plain muted brown clothing, seated at the questioning side, attentive and serious, hand raised slightly to ask their own question. No implied representation of all patients.
Left panel: Morlen is standing beside the patient's seating side, body beginning to turn away. Caregiver, positioned in the space between questioner's seat and separate witness stool, politely gestures toward that witness stool, not toward the exit. Patient holds the question space and is not touched.
Right panel: Morlen has moved to the distinctly separate side witness stool, seated angled toward patient, hands clear and visible in lap, not commanding the hearing. Patient remains in the SAME seat and now visibly leads the question with a restrained open-hand gesture. Caregiver stands slightly aside, leaving the visual line between patient and witness unobstructed.
CRITICAL PROP: a single CLOSED plain brown case notebook rests on a small low neutral stand BETWEEN the patient's seat and witness stool in BOTH panels. It remains untouched at precisely the same place, showing no identifying names, portrait, readable writing or exposed pages. Other private case names remain behind the locked cabinet. Do not let Morlen clutch or reclaim the notebook.
There is no chair at a grand head-of-table position, no throne, no handshake, no forgiveness, no triumphant smiles, no compensation payment, no medicine being administered, no patient restraint, no machine connected to bodies. Do not draw Verren or Gwynnel; their canonical appearances are not supplied. An empty seat must not be presented as consent or attendance. This is a conditional composition after independent care transfer and voluntary limited hearing authorization, NOT a claim that story state is completed.
Make the body-direction and seat change immediately legible while maintaining the free exit.

assets.fullPrompt:
Use case: illustration-story
Asset type: original pixel-art concept storyboard of readiness BEFORE a two-front rescue, NOT a playable map or completed rescue. 1536x1024 landscape.
Create exactly TWO distinct room panels side by side, separated by a very thick opaque charcoal gutter and separate visible cutaway room frames. The panels show the SAME preparedness moment at DIFFERENT elevations and non-contiguous locations. NO corridor, stair, pipe, water surface or floor may visually connect across the gutter. No words or text.
Style: dense hard-edged readable pixel clusters, three-quarter elevated RPG view, muted gray masonry, damp brown timber, dark teal still water, cream linen, subdued olive clothing, restrained warm lantern light. No glossy 3D, gradients or blur.
LEFT PANEL: independent lower refuge-door room segment. Two separate closed heavy timber refuge doors in the back wall, each with iron bands and a small dark barred window; no face visible through them. A broad dry stone ledge runs from doors to a clearly open ascending stone maintenance stair at far left, leading out of this panel. Two actual generic adult neutral caregivers are physically in place on the dry ledge: one in olive dress and brown apron holding folded cream linens, one in simple brown tunic with a small care satchel beside an empty folded litter leaned against wall. They stand to the SIDE of the walking path, ready to receive people; neither blocks doors, stair, or return route. They are not Mia, Toman or captive laborers. Keep water below ledge, calm and at the current fixed mechanism phase. No rescued workers outside, no drowned bodies, no researcher portrait.
RIGHT PANEL: a SEPARATE high records-maintenance shelter room, shown with its own stone enclosure and dry wood-and-stone floor. Exactly one anonymous adult player adventurer in dark neutral cloak, face not emphasized, stands at the optional-records station checking an open empty weatherproof wrapping case next to a modest stack of optional records. Hands poised to prepare protection, no carrying everything away, no finish gesture. A different CLOSED wall cabinet, clearly above flood exposure, holds the fixed safe copy independently; do not open, remove or combine it with optional records. Room has its OWN unobstructed dry return opening. A fixed bypass-valve wheel remains untouched on its mechanism, no person touches it, no spinning arrows, no opened rushing floodgate. Current water level is unchanged; readiness precedes operation.
Composition conveys real, limited human staffing and two distinct responsibilities. Caregivers have already agreed and been validly funded or arranged for this conditional concept, but don't show gold payments, contracts, approval icons or completed-state stamps. No victory, no everyone-rescued montage, no recruitment, no immunity, no forced relocation, no extra game UI, no countdown, no auto-rising water. Researcher and workers remain behind different lower doors; images make no health or survival claim. Do not place lower refuge doors in the high records room. The right high records room is a concept proposal, not a canonical adjacency or exact map.
